title: He didn’t just find treasure.
paragraphs: He exposed what he was willing to lose.

What if the reason you feel empty…
is not because God is absent—
…but because you’re still holding on to what He’s asking you to release?
There’s a man in the dust.

Sweat on his brow.
Dirt under his nails.
A life that looked… ordinary.
Until one moment broke everything open.
Something buried beneath what everyone else walked past.
His entire life became a decision.
This is where it gets uncomfortable.
Because the story of Matthew 13:44 is not soft.
“The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field, which a man found and covered up. Then in his joy he goes and sells all that he has and buys that field.” — Matthew 13:44 (ESV)
In his joy… he sold everything.

Not regret.
Not pressure.
Not obligation.
Most of us don’t feel joy when God starts touching our attachments.
we know what we’re clinging to.
That image you protect so no one sees the real you.
It’s costing you more than you admit.
The man didn’t accidentally own the treasure.
He had to choose it over everything else.
And this is where shame creeps in.
You knew it wasn’t right… but you stayed.
You felt the conviction… but you silenced it.
You heard God whisper… but you delayed obedience.
And now there’s this quiet weight inside you.
“You’ve already chosen wrong too many times.”
That is not the voice of Jesus.
Because the Gospel does not say:
“Sell everything perfectly, then come to Me.”
“You couldn’t afford the treasure… so I paid for you.”
Some scholars interpret this parable as the believer recognizing the infinite value of God’s Kingdom and surrendering everything in response.
Others see something even more staggering:
Jesus is the man in the story.
And He saw something hidden in it.
“Though He was rich, yet for your sake He became poor, so that you by His poverty might become rich.” — 2 Corinthians 8:9
The cross was not partial payment.
“God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
You are not the only one being asked to give everything.
But here’s the truth most people avoid:

You cannot hold on to your sin
and fully embrace the Kingdom.
But because sin will keep suffocating what He’s trying to revive.
“If anyone would come after Me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow Me.” — Luke 9:23
there’s something in your life you keep burying.
Hoping God will just… overlook it.
But He doesn’t expose to shame you.
The same God who sees your hidden sin…
Grace is powerful enough to break chains you thought were permanent.
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us… and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” — 1 John 1:9
What are you still holding onto?
That you already know is not worth the cost?
but because Jesus is worth more.
Free from the exhausting weight of trying to control everything.
Because the treasure was never the field.
Jesus is the treasure your soul has been searching for in everything else.
And receive what you could never earn.
you remember what’s truly worth everything.
